title: Annihilator calculus for submodules, quotients and exact complexes of sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal J,\mathcal K$ be quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], write $\mathcal J\mathcal F$ for the image of ideal multiplication [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Then (1) for any monomorphism $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, $\mathcal J\mathcal G=0$ implies $\mathcal J\mathcal F=0$; (2) for any epimorphism $\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, $\mathcal J\mathcal F=0$ implies $\mathcal J\mathcal G=0$; (3) for any complex $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ exact at $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], if $\mathcal J\mathcal A=0$ and $\mathcal K\mathcal C=0$, then $(\mathcal J\mathcal K)\mathcal B=0$.

source.place: Tag 0CYV, lemma-systems-with-proper-support, proof of (2), annihilator argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CYV

proof.text: Detect zero module sheaves on all module stalks. The faithful zero-preserving forgetful functor to abelian sheaves reflects zero objects by the identity-equals-zero criterion. Apply Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.isZero_iff_stalkFunctor_obj_isZero, then forget the stalk scalar structure through the faithful functor ModuleCat -> AddCommGrpCat. This is the fully proved private helper zero_iff_stalks.

Choose the structure-sheaf stalk identification supplied by ideal_module_product_stalk. Its product inclusion on stalks is injective. Use ideal_multiplication_stalk_range with this same identification for every ideal and every module: the range equals I times the top submodule. An injective map has zero source precisely when its range is bottom, and Submodule.smul_le says this is equivalent to r*m=0 for every r in I and every m. This proves product_stalk_zero_iff, including compatibility between different ideals without choosing different identifications.

A monomorphism is sectionwise injective by the faithful forgetful functor to module presheaves. The injectivity clause of module_stalk_exact makes its stalk maps injective. Naturality of scalar multiplication then transfers annihilation from target stalks to source stalks, so zero_iff_stalks proves clause (1).

For an epimorphism a:F -> G the short complex F -> G -> G whose second map is zero is exact, by ShortComplex.exact_iff_epi. The stalk exactness criterion in module_stalk_exact makes its stalk complex exact. ShortComplex.Exact.epi_f and ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective give surjectivity on stalks. Lift each target stalk element and use linearity to transfer annihilation from source to target, proving clause (2).

Identify membership in the stalk image ideal of J with being the germ of a section in J.ideal U for an affine neighborhood U. Represent the preimage stalk element by a section, restrict it to an affine neighborhood, and apply range_toModulesι_app and stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply. Conversely lift an affine ideal section with range_toModulesι_app and take its germ. These are the fully proved private helpers inclusion_stalk_germ and mem_stalkIdeal_iff, using the existing IdealSheaf.Module bridge.

Prove the stalk image ideal of J*K equals I_J*I_K. For the forward inclusion represent an element by an affine (J*K)-ideal section, use ideal_mul and Ideal.map_mul on its germ, and note that each mapped affine ideal lies in the corresponding stalk ideal by step 5. For the reverse inclusion apply Ideal.mul_le, represent both factors by affine ideal sections, restrict to a common affine neighborhood, use ideal_le_comap_ideal to retain membership, multiply there using Ideal.mul_mem_mul, and apply compatibility of germs with restriction and multiplication. This is the fully proved private helper stalkIdeal_mul; no extra theorem is assumed.

Map an exact complex A -> B -> C to each stalk using module_stalk_exact. For j in I_J, k in I_K and b in B_x, linearity and annihilation of C_x give g(k*b)=0. ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff supplies a with f(a)=k*b. Then (j*k)*b=j*f(a)=f(j*a)=0 by annihilation of A_x. Ideal.mul_le puts I_J*I_K in the annihilator of B_x. Steps 2 and 6 prove zero product stalks, and step 1 proves clause (3). Only middle exactness is used; no mono or epi condition on the outer maps is added.

lean.statement:
theorem idealModuleProduct_exact_calculus (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (∀ (J : X.IdealSheafData) {F G : X.Modules} (a : F ⟶ G) [Mono a],
      IsZero (idealModuleProduct J.toModulesι G) →
        IsZero (idealModuleProduct J.toModulesι F)) ∧
    (∀ (J : X.IdealSheafData) {F G : X.Modules} (a : F ⟶ G) [Epi a],
      IsZero (idealModuleProduct J.toModulesι F) →
        IsZero (idealModuleProduct J.toModulesι G)) ∧
    (∀ (J K : X.IdealSheafData) (T : ShortComplex X.Modules), T.Exact →
      IsZero (idealModuleProduct J.toModulesι T.X₁) →
      IsZero (idealModuleProduct K.toModulesι T.X₃) →
        IsZero (idealModuleProduct (J * K).toModulesι T.X₂))
